activity.notes: Frederick, later King Frederick I of Denmark and Norway, and his elder brother John were jointly accepted as dukes of Schleswig and Holstein in 1482 while Frederick was still a minor. In 1490 the ducal lands and revenues were partitioned; Frederick chose the Gottorp share and thereafter exercised personal ducal rule from Gottorf while the constitutional unity of Schleswig and Holstein and several common institutions were maintained under the co-dukes. ATLAS therefore begins his direct Schleswig-Holstein leadership in 1490 and records him as Co-Duke rather than treating the duchies as a unitary modern state.

sources.title: Friedrich I. von Dänemark — Deutsche Biographie
sources.citation_text: Neue Deutsche Biographie identifies Frederick I as Duke of Schleswig-Holstein and later King of Denmark-Norway, explaining the 1482 joint homage and the 1490 partition in which Frederick chose the Gottorp share while common institutions of the duchies remained joint.

sources.title: From Margrethe to Frederik: Danish history as told by royal lines — University of Copenhagen
sources.citation_text: The University of Copenhagen reproduces an early-modern chronicle identifying Frederik I as Duke in Schleswig and Holstein before he succeeded to the Danish crown.
